1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
148	change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289	
290	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
291	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
292	  as **memory**.
293	
294	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
295	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
297	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
298	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
299	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
300	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
301	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
302	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309	
310	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
312	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
315	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
319	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
320	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
327	
328	## Final report (your last message)
329	
330	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
331	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
332	Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
333	`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
334	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
335	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
336	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
337	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
338	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
339	not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.
340	
341	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
342	
343	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
344	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
345	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
346	`subagents` skill):
347	
348	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
349	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
350	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
351	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
352	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
353	
354	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DegreeZero
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap

/-!
# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)

For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## The degree at a field point -/

/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))

section DegAt

variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]

/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
@[simp]
theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]

/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]

/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
  rfl

/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
  rw [← picEtMap_comp]

/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'

end DegAt

/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/

variable (C) in
/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
    degAt lam t = 0}
  one_mem' := by
    intro K _ _ t
    exact degAt_one t
  mul_mem' := by
    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
  inv_mem' := by
    intro a ha K _ _ t
    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]

/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
          degAt lam t = 0 :=
  Iff.rfl

variable (C) in
/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
points. -/
def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))

naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/

theorem descentMap_congr {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}

    descentMap C h₁ x = descentMap C h₂ x :=

/-! ## The plus construction -/

/-- Two descent-class representatives are identified when they agree after transport to a
common refinement.  By `descentMap_congr` the choice of transport maps is immaterial, so
the relation is an equivalence (directedness of covers gives transitivity). -/
instance picEtAffSetoid : Setoid (Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E) where
  r p q := ∃ (F : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : p.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
    (g : q.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier), descentMap C f p.2 = descentMap C g q.2

relative Picard classes on some presented étale cover satisfying the descent condition,
modulo agreement on a common refinement.  On affine tests this *is* the étale
sheafification of the relative Picard presheaf (one plus suffices because the presheaf is
étale-separated — proved separately). -/

variable (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))

/-- The compatible families over the affine opens of the test object, as a subgroup of
the product of the affine-level plus groups: the value at a smaller affine open is the
restriction of the value at a larger one. -/
def picEtSubgroup :
    Subgroup (Π U : T.left.affineOpens, PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1)) where
  carrier := {s | ∀ (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1),
    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s V) = s U}
  one_mem' := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, map_one]
  mul_mem' {a b} ha hb := fun U V h => by
    rw [Pi.mul_apply, Pi.mul_apply, map_mul, ha U V h, hb U V h]
  inv_mem' {a} ha := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.inv_apply, Pi.inv_apply, map_inv, ha U V h]

/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor at an arbitrary test object**, object
level: compatible families of affine-level plus classes over the affine opens of
`T.left` — the bespoke affine-opens limit of `PicEtAff C ∘ Γ(T.left, ·)`.  On affine
tests this is `PicEtAff` itself (`picEtAffineEquiv`); on general tests it is its
canonical Zariski-continuous extension. -/
def picEt : Type u :=
  picEtSubgroup C T

noncomputable instance : CommGroup (picEt C T) :=
  inferInstanceAs (CommGroup (picEtSubgroup C T))

namespace picEt

variable {C T}

/-- The compatibility of a section of `picEt` along an inclusion of affine opens. -/
lemma compat (s : picEt C T) (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1) :
    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s.1 V) = s.1 U :=
  s.2 U V h

@[ext]
lemma ext {s t : picEt C T} (h : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens, s.1 U = t.1 U) : s = t :=
  Subtype.ext (funext h)

variable (C T) in
/-- Evaluation of a section of `picEt` at an affine open, as a group homomorphism. -/
def eval (U : T.left.affineOpens) : picEt C T →* PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1) :=
  (Pi.evalMonoidHom (fun V : T.left.affineOpens => PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, V.1)) U).comp
    (picEtSubgroup C T).subtype

@[simp]
lemma eval_apply (U : T.left.affineOpens) (s : picEt C T) : eval C T U s = s.1 U :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma mul_val (s t : picEt C T) (U : T.left.affineOpens) :
    (s * t).1 U = s.1 U * t.1 U :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma one_val (U : T.left.affineOpens) : (1 : picEt C T).1 U = 1 :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma inv_val (s : picEt C T) (U : T.left.affineOpens) : (s⁻¹).1 U = (s.1 U)⁻¹ :=

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
open AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme (CechPic)

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))

noncomputable section

/-- The subgroup of Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` pulled back from the test object `T`
along the second projection. The relative Picard group is the quotient by it. -/
def picFromBase (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup ((C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :=
  (CechPic.map (snd C T).left).range

lemma mem_picFromBase_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
    L ∈ picFromBase C T ↔ ∃ N : T.left.CechPic, CechPic.map (snd C T).left N = L :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The relative Picard group of `C/k` at a test object `T`: Picard classes on `C ⊗ T`
modulo classes pulled back from `T`. -/
def relPic (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
  (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic ⧸ picFromBase C T

noncomputable instance (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : CommGroup (relPic C T) :=
  QuotientGroup.Quotient.commGroup (picFromBase C T)

/-- The projection from Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` to the relative Picard group. -/
noncomputable def relPicMk (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic →* relPic C T :=
  QuotientGroup.mk' (picFromBase C T)

lemma relPicMk_surjective (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    Function.Surjective (relPicMk C T) :=
  QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective (picFromBase C T)

/-- The exact coset relation: two Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` have equal image in the
relative Picard group iff their ratio is pulled back from `T`. -/
lemma relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    {L L' : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
    relPicMk C T L = relPicMk C T L' ↔ L / L' ∈ picFromBase C T :=
  QuotientGroup.eq_iff_div_mem

@[elab_as_elim]
theorem relPic.ind {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {motive : relPic C T → Prop}
    (mk : ∀ L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic, motive (relPicMk C T L)) (x : relPic C T) :
    motive x :=
  QuotientGroup.induction_on x mk

variable {T T' T'' : Over (Spec (.of k))}

/-- Pullback of Čech Picard classes along `C ◁ g` sends classes from `T` to classes
from `T'`: the well-definedness of `relPicMap` on the `H_T`-cosets. -/
lemma picFromBase_le_comap (g : T' ⟶ T) :
    picFromBase C T ≤ (picFromBase C T').comap (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) := by
  rintro _ ⟨N, rfl⟩
  refine ⟨CechPic.map g.left N, ?_⟩
  show CechPic.map (snd C T').left (CechPic.map g.left N)
      = CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left (CechPic.map (snd C T).left N)
  rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp,
    ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left, ← Over.comp_left, whiskerLeft_snd]

/-- Restriction of relative Picard classes along `g : T' ⟶ T`: pull back along
`C ◁ g` and descend to the quotients. -/
noncomputable def relPicMap (g : T' ⟶ T) : relPic C T →* relPic C T' :=
  QuotientGroup.map (picFromBase C T) (picFromBase C T')
    (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) (picFromBase_le_comap C g)

@[simp]

**Three** roadmap rows defer to one sentence — *"inhabitation of the pair `(huniv V, hcov V)`
is UNMEASURED at every `V` and may be empty everywhere"* — namely `AJCR.w4-rep`,

exactly one other file, `Pic0ChartSeamCollapse.lean:13`, from which the paragraph you are

three** — `Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean:107` says the materially weaker "no measured inhabitant at
any `V`".  Corrected because inflating the count inflates what this file unblocks.)

Every predecessor result is an *endpoint* result — the pair's coverage clause is refuted at
`V = ⊥`, antecedent 1 is free there, and antecedent 1 is maximal at `V = ⊤` — and
`Pic0ChartSeamCollapse` identifies the pair with `IsIso` of the chart map without exhibiting
or refuting one.

**This file decides it.**  At the chart whose `rep` slot is filled by the landed degree-zero
producer, the pair is *equivalent* to a hypothesis that already has a name elsewhere in the
tree:

  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f ∧ IsLocallySurjective f  ↔  ∀ S, Subsingleton (pic⁰(S))`

Both directions, with no `V`-restriction, no chart index constraint beyond the free `hdeg` at
parameter `0`, and no hypothesis on the curve beyond its standing package.

## Why this parameter, and why it is not a degenerate dodge

The chart is `abelSigmaChartZero` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUseSite.lean`), the Abel
chart at parameter `0`, whose `rep` binder is discharged by `divFunctorZeroRepresentableBy`.
Its source is the representing object's underlying scheme — and at parameter `0` that object
is the *terminal* `Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k))`, so the source is `Spec k` itself and the chart map
sends a point `v : T ⟶ Spec k` to the Σ-element `⟨v, class⟩`.

That shape is what makes both directions cheap, and in *opposite* ways:

* **Antecedent 1 is free**, because the Σ-component of the chart value **is** the point:
  reading it off recovers `v`, so the map is injective on the nose at every test
  (`injective_abelSigmaChartZero`).  This is not the `V = ⊥` degeneracy — the source is
  nonempty and the statement is at the unrestricted chart.
* **Antecedent 2 is exactly the vanishing**, because the Σ-component is *surjective* for free
  and the fibre component then has to be hit, which at a singleton `pic⁰` it is
  (`surjective_app_abelSigmaChartZero_of_subsingleton`).  Conversely a *second* degree-zero
  class at one test defeats surjectivity, so the vanishing is not merely sufficient
  (`subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_surjective_app`).

`Picard/Pic0VanishingRoute.lean` produces `JacobianData` from by a route with *none* of the
atlas's antecedents.  The two routes are not alternatives: they close together.

`Pic0ChartSeamCollapse.chartIso_of_seam` takes `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` and extracts
injectivity from it via `IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms`.  Here injectivity is available

weaker input (`chartIso_of_injective`).  That restatement has an independent payoff, recorded

elementwise injectivity** — the two-clause `MorphismProperty.relative` reading that

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DegreeZero
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap
8	
9	/-!
10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
11	
12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
33	-/
34	
35	set_option autoImplicit false
36	
37	universe u
38	
39	open CategoryTheory
40	
41	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
42	
43	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
44	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
45	
46	noncomputable section
47	
48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
49	
50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
57	
58	section DegAt
59	
60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
61	
62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
63	@[simp]
64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
67	
68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
75	
76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
81	  rfl
82	
83	/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
84	restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
85	field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
86	degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
87	theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
88	    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
89	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
90	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
91	  rw [← picEtMap_comp]
92	
93	/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
94	theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
95	    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
96	    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
97	  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'
98	
99	end DegAt
100	
101	/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/
102	
103	variable (C) in
104	/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
105	classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
106	degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
107	def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
108	  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
109	    degAt lam t = 0}
110	  one_mem' := by
111	    intro K _ _ t
112	    exact degAt_one t
113	  mul_mem' := by
114	    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
115	    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
116	  inv_mem' := by
117	    intro a ha K _ _ t
118	    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]
119	
120	/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
121	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
122	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
123	      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
124	          degAt lam t = 0 :=
125	  Iff.rfl
126	
127	variable (C) in
128	/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
129	of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
130	definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
131	points. -/
132	def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
133	    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
134	  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
135	    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))
136	
137	/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
138	naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
139	@[simp]
140	theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
141	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
142	    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
143	  rfl
144	
145	variable (C) in
146	/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
147	subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
148	of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
149	the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
150	functor. -/
151	def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
152	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
153	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)
154	  map_id T := by
155	    ext lam U
156	    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
157	  map_comp g h := by
158	    ext lam U
159	    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))
160	
161	@[simp]
162	theorem pic0Functor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
163	    (pic0Functor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :=
164	  rfl
165	
166	@[simp]
167	theorem pic0Functor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
168	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
169	    (pic0Functor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
170	  rfl
171	
172	variable (C) in
173	/-- The inclusion of the degree-zero subfunctor into the étale-sheafified relative
174	Picard functor, as a natural transformation — the naturality square consumers cite
175	(bundled form of `pic0Map_coe`). -/
176	def pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C where
177	  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Subgroup C T.unop).subtype
178	  naturality _ _ _ := rfl
179	
180	end
181

32	  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
34	  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
35	  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
36	  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
37	  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
38	  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
39	  Σ-component of the universal element.
40	-/

42	set_option autoImplicit false
43	
44	universe u
45	
46	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
47	
48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
49	
50	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
51	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
52	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
53	
54	/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/
55	
56	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
57	massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
58	noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
59	  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat
60	
61	@[simp]
62	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
63	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj T = pic0Subgroup C T.unop :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
67	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
68	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
69	  rfl
70	
71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)
78	
79	variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
80	
81	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)
103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
112	    intro p
113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
130	  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
134	    exact hs i
135	  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
137	    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
140	    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
141	      (ht' i)
142	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem
143	
144	/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
145	big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
146	consumes. -/
147	noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
148	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
149	    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩
150	
151	/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/
152	
153	/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
155	certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
156	through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
157	type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
158	Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
159	`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
160	element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
161	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
162	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
163	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
164	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
165	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
166	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
167	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
168	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
169	  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice
170	
171	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise
7	
8	/-!
9	# B-5 at the Abel chart: what the pointwise datum unfolds to, and what it costs
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` reduces `ChartsCoverLocally` — hence B-6 — to a
12	four-part datum at each point of each test.  That reduction is stated for an *arbitrary*
13	family of presheaf maps, so it says nothing about how hard the datum is at the family that
14	matters.  This file instantiates it at `abelSigmaChart` and computes the answer.
15	
16	## The computation, and the one thing it makes visible
17	
18	A section of `pic0SigmaSheaf C` over a **bare** test scheme `T` is by definition a *pair*
19	`⟨a, λ⟩` with `a : T ⟶ Spec k` and `λ` a degree-zero class on the slice object `Over.mk a`
20	(`Over.sigmaExtension`, `Picard/OverSigmaExtension.lean`).  And `(Over.mk a).left` is `T`
21	itself, definitionally.  So the big-site/slice crossing that looks like it needs a bridge does
22	not: the pointwise datum's `t : ↥T` *is* a point of the slice test, and `chartLocus` applies to
23	it with no transport.  `abelChartApp_eq` below records the crossing as an equation rather than
24	leaving it to unfold at a use site.
25	
26	What the computation *does* make visible is where the cost sits.  `abelSigmaChart`'s value at
27	`x : W ⟶ D.left` is `⟨x ≫ D.hom, chartValue … (rep.homEquiv …)⟩`, so matching it against the
28	restriction of `⟨a, λ⟩` needs **both** components: the Σ-component is an equation between
29	morphisms to `Spec k`, and only then is there a class equation.  A producer that supplies the
30	class half alone has not supplied the datum — the Σ-component is what pins the chart point to
31	lie *over* the test, and it is free only because `W.ι ≫ a` is what `D.hom` must equal.
32	
33	## THE CORRECTION THIS FILE CARRIES, against this lane's own headline
34	
35	`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:40` says of its `chartLocusOpens`:
36	
37	> `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised — the `W` field costs zero, which is
38	> a real reduction of the datum from four fields to three
39	
40	**The second clause is false, and the roadmap `c9b` row repeats it** ("`W` needs nothing").
41	`chartLocusOpens` takes an argument `haff`, the affine-local openness of the locus at every
42	affine open of the test, and *nothing in the tree discharges it*:
43	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsoInvariance.lean`) removed the
44	`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis and passes `haff` straight through, as does
45	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it.  The affine case that would feed it is
46	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`), which is
47	itself conditional on `IsChartDatumPresentation` — B-4's *named residue*.
48	
49	**Update, same session** (`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`): that residue is now
50	*entirely witness-free*.  Its forward half already was (the trivial splitting), and its
51	converse `hconv` — the descent direction, open for three sessions — is discharged by plus-unit
52	injectivity.  So what `haff` ultimately costs is a `cechPicClass` base-change identity: no
53	witness, no `H¹`, no divisor, and nothing certificate- or divRep-gated.
54	
55	So the honest accounting is: **`W` costs `haff`, which costs B-4's presentation residue.**  The
56	datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  What is
57	genuinely free is the type-level crossing above, and `chartLocusHaff` below is the residue
58	named so it cannot be lost again.
59	
60	## Main declarations
61	
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelChartApp_eq` — the Abel chart's value at a point of the divisor
63	  scheme, as an explicit `Sigma.mk`.  Both components, since the datum needs both.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartLocusAffineLocal` — the `haff` residue, named.  This is what
65	  `chartLocusOpens` silently costs.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens_of_affineLocal` — `chartLocusOpens` from it, so the
67	  dependency is explicit in the API rather than in an argument position.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation` — the residue **reduced to B-4's
69	  own named obligation**: a per-affine-piece `IsChartDatumPresentation` gives it.  This is the
70	  link that was asserted in `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring and never written.
71	-/
72	
73	set_option autoImplicit false
74	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
75	
76	universe u
77	
78	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
79	
80	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
81	
82	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
83	
84	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
85	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
86	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
87	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
88	
89	noncomputable section
90	
91	/-! ## The Abel chart's value, both components -/
92	
93	/-- **The Abel chart map evaluated at a point of the divisor scheme.**
94	
95	`abelSigmaChart` is `rep.toSigmaExtension ≫ Over.sigmaExtensionNat (chartValueTrans …)`, and
96	both factors act componentwise on the Σ-extension, so the value at `x : Y ⟶ D.left` is the
97	pair whose structure morphism is `x ≫ D.hom` and whose class is the chart value of the divisor
98	family `rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)`.
99	
100	Recorded as an equation because a coverage producer has to match this against a *given*
101	section, and the match is two equations rather than one: the Σ-components must agree before
102	the classes are even in the same type.  Leaving it to unfold at the use site is how the
103	Σ-component gets forgotten. -/
104	@[simp]
105	theorem abelChartApp_eq {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
106	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
108	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
109	    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (x : Y ⟶ D.left) :
110	    (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app (op Y) x
111	      = ⟨x ≫ D.hom, ⟨chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x ≫ D.hom))
112	          (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)),
113	        chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg _ _⟩⟩ :=
114	  rfl
115	
116	/-! ## The `haff` residue, named
117	
118	`chartLocusOpens` takes the affine-local openness as an argument.  Naming it is not cosmetic:
119	an argument in a definition's signature is invisible to a census of open obligations, which is
120	how "the `W` field costs zero" survived into two roadmap rows. -/
121	
122	variable (C) in
123	/-- **The affine-local openness residue of `chartLocus`** — what `chartLocusOpens` costs.
124	
125	For a test `T` and a class `lam` on it, this says the chart locus is open over every affine
126	open piece of `T`.  It is exactly the `haff` argument of `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'`,
127	and it is the *only* remaining input to CHART-U(b) at a general test: the iso-invariance
128	hypothesis that used to sit beside it was discharged
129	(`isSplitWitnessIsoInvariant_holds`), but this one was passed through, not proved.
130	
131	Named as a `Prop` so that it appears in searches for open obligations. -/
132	def ChartLocusAffineLocal (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
133	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : Prop :=
134	  ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
135	    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))
136	
137	variable (C) in
138	/-- `chartLocusOpens` with its cost made explicit in the API.
139	
140	Identical in content to `chartLocusOpens` — the point is that the dependency is now a named
141	`Prop` a reader can grep for, rather than an unnamed argument that reads as bookkeeping. -/
142	def chartLocusOpens' (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
143	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
144	    (haff : ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam) : T.left.Opens :=
145	  chartLocusOpens C m Z T lam haff
146	
147	@[simp]
148	lemma mem_chartLocusOpens' {m : ℕ} {Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor}
149	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} {haff : ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam}
150	    {t : T.left} :
151	    t ∈ chartLocusOpens' C m Z T lam haff ↔ t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam :=
152	  Iff.rfl
153	
154	/-! ## Reducing the residue to B-4's own named obligation
155	
156	`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`'s docstring says the general-test statement follows from the
157	affine one "by the affine-piece locality of the (b-amendment)'s transport (iii)", and adds that
158	it "is not stated here only because it would need the presentation hypothesis *per affine
159	piece*".  That is right, and this is the statement it describes. -/
160	
161	set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in
162	variable (C π) in
163	/-- **The `haff` residue from a per-affine-piece presentation** — the link
164	`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring describes and does not state.
165	
166	For each affine open `U` of the test, a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `Γ(T.left, U)` presenting
167	the restricted twisted class gives openness of the locus on that piece
168	(`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation`), and `chartLocus` over the piece *is* that set
169	by definition (`chartLocus` unfolds to the split-witness set of the twisted class, and the
170	twist commutes with restriction by `picEtMap_chartTwist`).
171	
172	So the affine-local residue is **exactly** B-4's presentation obligation, quantified over
173	affine pieces — no extra geometry, and in particular nothing certificate- or divRep-gated.
174	Combined with `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` this closes CHART-U(b) at a general test the
175	moment `IsChartDatumPresentation` is available per piece.
176	
177	The `hπ` and `IsFinite π` hypotheses are the ones
178	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` carries.  `IsFinite π` is strictly stronger than
179	the file-level `IsAffineHom π` (whence the overlapping-instance warning, disabled below): the
180	affine openness route runs through the rigid engine, which needs finiteness, while the rest of
181	this file needs only affineness. -/
182	theorem chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation [IsFinite π]
183	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
184	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
185	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
186	    (hpres : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
187	      ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C (Γ(T.left, U.1)) π,
188	        IsChartDatumPresentation C π
189	          (chartTwist C m Z _ (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)) D) :
190	    ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam := by
191	  intro U
192	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := hpres U
193	  exact isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation C π hπ hD
194	
195	end
196	
197	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	/-!
10	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor on all test objects: the object level
11	
12	For a curve `C` over `k`, the étale-sheafified relative Picard group of an **affine**
13	test is the one-step plus construction `PicEtAff C A` (étale-separatedness of the
14	relative Picard presheaf makes one plus suffice — axiom (C1),
15	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.CechKernelLemma`).  The frozen group-object interface forces
16	the functor to exist on **all** of `Over (Spec k)`; following the resolution of the
17	Layer-2 vehicle question (inbox I-0140), the extension is the *bespoke affine-opens
18	limit*: a section over a test object `T` is a compatible family of plus classes over the
19	affine opens of `T.left`, valued in `PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U)` via the section-ring
20	algebras of `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtSections`.  The index poset is `Type u`-small,
21	which is the point of the vehicle.
22	
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEt C T`: the limit, as the subgroup of the product over
24	  `T.left.affineOpens` cut out by compatibility under restriction, with its `CommGroup`
25	  structure; `picEt.eval` is evaluation at an affine open.
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.congr C e`: transport of plus classes along an isomorphism
27	  of test algebras.
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtAffineEquiv C A`: **the affine comparison** — on an affine
29	  test `overSpec k A`, evaluation at the top affine open is a group isomorphism
30	  `picEt C (overSpec k A) ≃* PicEtAff C A` (the affine-opens poset of an affine test has
31	  a terminal element, so the limit collapses).
32	
33	Functoriality in `T` — restriction along an arbitrary morphism of test objects, by
34	gluing over basic-open refinements, licensed by (C1)-separatedness — is built on top of
35	the Zariski sheaf property of `PicEtAff` in `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap`.
36	-/
37	
38	set_option autoImplicit false
39	
40	universe u
41	
42	open CategoryTheory
43	
44	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
45	
46	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
47	
48	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra
49	
50	noncomputable section
51	
52	/-! ## Transport of plus classes along an isomorphism of test algebras -/
53	
54	namespace PicEtAff
55	
56	variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
57	
58	/-- Transport of étale-plus Picard classes along an isomorphism of test algebras. -/
59	def congr (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) : PicEtAff C A ≃* PicEtAff C B where
60	  toFun := mapAlg C e.toAlgHom

14	étale-separated, by descent — proved separately): a class of the plus is represented by a
15	relative Picard class on an étale cover `Spec B → Spec A` equipped with a *descent
16	condition* — equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double cover
17	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B)` — and two representatives are identified when they agree on a common
18	refinement.
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentClasses C E`: the subgroup of `relPic C (Spec B)` of classes
21	  satisfying the descent condition on the cover `E` with carrier `B`.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap C h`: transport of descent classes along a refinement map
23	  `h` of covers.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap_congr` (**the keystone**): a descent class restricts
25	  equally along any two `A`-algebra maps out of the cover carrier — the pair `(j₁, j₂)`
26	  factors through the double cover, where the descent condition kills the difference.
27	  Specialized to refinement maps as `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap_congr`, this is what
28	  makes the colimit below independent of all choices; applied across base rings
29	  (`Picard/PicEtAffMap.lean`), it is also what makes the plus functorial in the test
30	  algebra.
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff C A`: the one-step plus — descent classes on some cover,
32	  modulo agreement on a common refinement — with its `CommGroup` structure and the
33	  constructor/eliminator API `PicEtAff.mk`, `PicEtAff.ind`, `PicEtAff.mk_eq_mk_iff`,
34	  `PicEtAff.mk_descentMap`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.unit`: the unit `relPic C (Spec A) →* PicEtAff C A` of the
36	  plus construction — a class pulled back to the trivial cover with its tautological
37	  descent datum.
38	
39	The functoriality of `PicEtAff` in `A` (restriction along test maps, via base change of
40	covers) and the comparison theorems (injectivity of the unit = separatedness; bijectivity
41	under a section = rigidification) are subsequent layers, consuming only this interface.
42	-/

59	/-! ## Descent classes on an étale cover -/
60	
61	/-- The first coprojection from the carrier of a cover into its self-tensor product over
62	the base — the algebra face of the first projection of the double cover
63	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B) → Spec B` — as a `k`-algebra map. -/
64	def doubleInl (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
65	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
66	  Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
67	
68	/-- The second coprojection into the self-tensor product; see `doubleInl`. -/
69	def doubleInr (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
70	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
71	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight).restrictScalars k
72	
73	/-- The subgroup of relative Picard classes on an étale cover of the test algebra
74	satisfying the descent condition: equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double
75	cover. -/
76	def descentClasses (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
77	    Subgroup (relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
78	  MonoidHom.eqLocus
79	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E))
80	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E))
81	
82	lemma mem_descentClasses_iff {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
83	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} :
84	    x ∈ descentClasses C E ↔
85	      relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x
86	        = relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E) x :=
87	  Iff.rfl

90	
91	private lemma doubleInl_comp {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
92	    (doubleInl F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)
93	      = ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) := by
94	  ext x
95	  simp [doubleInl]
96	
97	private lemma doubleInr_comp {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
98	    (doubleInr F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)
99	      = ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E) := by
100	  ext x
101	  simp [doubleInr]
102	
103	/-- The descent condition is natural in the cover: pullback along a refinement map sends
104	descent classes to descent classes. -/
105	lemma relPicAlgMap_mem_descentClasses {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
106	    (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)}
107	    (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
108	    relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x ∈ descentClasses C F := by
109	  rw [mem_descentClasses_iff] at hx ⊢
110	  calc relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x)
111	      = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInl F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x :=
112	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
113	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
114	          (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [doubleInl_comp h]
115	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
116	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) := relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x
117	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
118	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by rw [hx]
119	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
120	          (doubleInr E)) x := (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
121	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInr F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x := by
122	        rw [doubleInr_comp h]
123	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x) :=
124	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x
125	
126	/-- Transport of descent classes along a refinement map of covers. -/
127	def descentMap {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
128	    descentClasses C E →* descentClasses C F :=
129	  ((relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k)).comp (descentClasses C E).subtype).codRestrict _
130	    fun x => relPicAlgMap_mem_descentClasses C h x.2

132	@[simp]
133	lemma descentMap_coe {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
134	    (x : descentClasses C E) :
135	    (descentMap C h x : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier))
136	      = relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
137	  rfl

139	@[simp]
140	lemma descentMap_id {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (x : descentClasses C E) :
141	    descentMap C (AlgHom.id A E.Carrier) x = x := by
142	  ext
143	  rw [descentMap_coe,
144	    show (AlgHom.id A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k = AlgHom.id k E.Carrier from rfl]
145	  exact relPicAlgMap_id C _
146	
147	lemma descentMap_comp {E F G : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
148	    (h' : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier) (x : descentClasses C E) :
149	    descentMap C (h'.comp h) x = descentMap C h' (descentMap C h x) := by
150	  ext
151	  rw [descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe,
152	    show (h'.comp h).restrictScalars k
153	      = (h'.restrictScalars k).comp (h.restrictScalars k) from rfl]
154	  exact relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _

156	/-- **Generalized refinement-map independence**, the keystone of the plus construction:
157	a class satisfying the descent condition restricts equally along any two `A`-algebra maps
158	out of the cover carrier — into an arbitrary test algebra, not merely another cover.  The
159	pair `(j₁, j₂)` factors jointly through the double cover of the source, where the descent
160	condition identifies the two pullbacks. -/
161	theorem relPicAlgMap_congr {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
162	    [Algebra k R] [Algebra A R] [IsScalarTower k A R] (j₁ j₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R)
163	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
164	    relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by
165	  set H : E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R :=
166	    Algebra.TensorProduct.lift j₁ j₂ fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _ with hH
167	  have key₁ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) = j₁.restrictScalars k := by
168	    ext y
169	    simp [hH, doubleInl]
170	  have key₂ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E) = j₂.restrictScalars k := by
171	    ext y
172	    simp [hH, doubleInr]
173	  calc relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x
174	      = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [key₁]
175	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) :=
176	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _
177	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by
178	        have hx' : relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x
179	            = relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E) x := hx
180	        rw [hx']
181	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E)) x :=
182	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _).symm
183	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by rw [key₂]
184	
185	/-- **Refinement-map independence**: any two refinement maps between the same covers
186	transport descent classes identically — what makes the plus construction independent of
187	all choices. -/
188	theorem descentMap_congr {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
189	    (h₁ h₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) (x : descentClasses C E) :
190	    descentMap C h₁ x = descentMap C h₂ x :=
191	  Subtype.ext (relPicAlgMap_congr C h₁ h₂ x.2)
192	
193	/-! ## The plus construction -/
194	
195	/-- Two descent-class representatives are identified when they agree after transport to a
196	common refinement.  By `descentMap_congr` the choice of transport maps is immaterial, so
197	the relation is an equivalence (directedness of covers gives transitivity). -/
198	instance picEtAffSetoid : Setoid (Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E) where
199	  r p q := ∃ (F : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : p.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
200	    (g : q.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier), descentMap C f p.2 = descentMap C g q.2
201	  iseqv := by
202	    constructor
203	    · exact fun p => ⟨p.1, AlgHom.id A _, AlgHom.id A _, rfl⟩
204	    · rintro p q ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩
205	      exact ⟨F, g, f, hfg.symm⟩
206	    · rintro p q r ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩ ⟨G, f', g', hfg'⟩
207	      refine ⟨F.prod G, (F.prodInl G).comp f, (F.prodInr G).comp g', ?_⟩
208	      rw [descentMap_comp, descentMap_comp, hfg, ← descentMap_comp, ← descentMap_comp,
209	        descentMap_congr C ((F.prodInl G).comp g) ((F.prodInr G).comp f') q.2,
210	        descentMap_comp, hfg', ← descentMap_comp]

214	relative Picard classes on some presented étale cover satisfying the descent condition,
215	modulo agreement on a common refinement.  On affine tests this *is* the étale
216	sheafification of the relative Picard presheaf (one plus suffices because the presheaf is
217	étale-separated — proved separately). -/
218	def PicEtAff : Type u :=
219	  Quotient (picEtAffSetoid C (A := A))

235	theorem mk_eq_mk_iff {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {x : descentClasses C E}
236	    {y : descentClasses C F} :
237	    mk C E x = mk C F y ↔
238	      ∃ (G : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier)
239	        (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier), descentMap C f x = descentMap C g y :=

244	theorem mk_descentMap {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
245	    (x : descentClasses C E) : mk C F (descentMap C h x) = mk C E x :=
246	  Quotient.sound ⟨F, AlgHom.id A F.Carrier, h, by rw [descentMap_id]⟩

250	/-- Transport through a `prodLift` collapses on the left factor. -/
251	lemma descentMap_prodLift_inl {E F H : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
252	    (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier) (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier)
253	    (x : descentClasses C E) :
254	    descentMap C (Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift f g) (descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x)
255	      = descentMap C f x := by
256	  rw [← descentMap_comp, Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift_comp_prodInl]

259	lemma descentMap_prodLift_inr {E F H : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
260	    (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier) (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier)
261	    (y : descentClasses C F) :
262	    descentMap C (Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift f g) (descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y)
263	      = descentMap C g y := by
264	  rw [← descentMap_comp, Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift_comp_prodInr]

267	-- The `rw` chain unifies `descentMap` nests whose `AlgHom` instance arguments run through
268	-- quotient and tensor-product carriers; the unifications are heartbeat-hungry.
269	private lemma mulLift_compat (p q p' q' : Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E)
270	    (hp : p ≈ p') (hq : q ≈ q') :
271	    mk C (p.1.prod q.1)
272	        (descentMap C (p.1.prodInl q.1) p.2 * descentMap C (p.1.prodInr q.1) q.2)
273	      = mk C (p'.1.prod q'.1)
274	        (descentMap C (p'.1.prodInl q'.1) p'.2
275	          * descentMap C (p'.1.prodInr q'.1) q'.2) := by
276	  obtain ⟨F, f, f', hf⟩ := hp
277	  obtain ⟨G, g, g', hg⟩ := hq
278	  refine (mk_eq_mk_iff C).mpr ⟨F.prod G,
279	    Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift ((F.prodInl G).comp f) ((F.prodInr G).comp g),
280	    Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift ((F.prodInl G).comp f') ((F.prodInr G).comp g'), ?_⟩
281	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, descentMap_prodLift_inl, descentMap_prodLift_inr,
282	    descentMap_prodLift_inl, descentMap_prodLift_inr, descentMap_comp, descentMap_comp,
283	    descentMap_comp, descentMap_comp, hf, hg]

292	    (y : descentClasses C F) :

294	      = mk C (E.prod F)

298	/-- Multiplication of two classes represented on the *same* cover is represented by the
299	product on that cover — the descent condition makes the two transports to the common
300	refinement agree. -/
301	theorem mk_mul_mk_same (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x y : descentClasses C E) :
302	    mk C E x * mk C E y = mk C E (x * y) := by
303	  have h : descentMap C (E.prodInl E) x * descentMap C (E.prodInl E) y
304	      = descentMap C (E.prodInl E) (x * y) :=
305	    (map_mul _ x y).symm
306	  rw [mk_mul_mk, descentMap_congr C (E.prodInr E) (E.prodInl E) y, h, mk_descentMap]

348	    rw [one_def, mk_mul_mk, map_one, one_mul, mk_descentMap]

357	    induction b using ind with | _ F y =>
358	    rw [← mk_descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x, ← mk_descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y,

363	/-- Every class pulled back from the base carries the tautological descent datum: the two
364	composites `A → B ⇉ B ⊗[A] B` coincide. -/
365	lemma tautological_mem_descentClasses (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A)
366	    (x : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
367	    relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) x
368	      ∈ descentClasses C E := by
369	  rw [mem_descentClasses_iff, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, ← relPicAlgMap_comp]
370	  congr 2
371	  ext a
372	  simp [doubleInl, doubleInr, Algebra.ofId_apply]
373	
374	variable (A) in
375	/-- The unit of the plus construction: a relative Picard class of the affine test,
376	pulled back to the trivial cover with its tautological descent datum. -/
377	def unit : relPic C (overSpec k A) →* PicEtAff C A where
378	  toFun x := mk C (.self A)
379	    ⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) x⟩
380	  map_one' := by
381	    rw [show (⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) 1⟩ :
382	        descentClasses C (.self A)) = 1 from Subtype.ext (map_one _), mk_one]
383	  map_mul' x y := by
384	    rw [show (⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) (x * y)⟩ :
385	        descentClasses C (.self A))
386	        = ⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) x⟩
387	          * ⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) y⟩ from
388	      Subtype.ext (map_mul _ x y), ← mk_mul_mk_same]
